test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following components in the axle is the most likely to fail if there is an unusual loud clanking or clunking as you put your vehicle into gear, or if a vehicle seems to struggle to get power as it starts to move?

options.text: Bearing at the wheel is damaged
There is a crack initiated in the axle at cross sectional area perpendicular to axis

solution:
The correct answer is __Axle-joint damage**(Option 4)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Axle-joint damage__ can result in loud clanking or clunking noises when the vehicle is put into gear.
 
• It may also cause the vehicle to struggle to get power as it starts to move.
 
• The axle joint connects the axle to the wheel and enables smooth rotation.
 
• Damage or wear in the axle joint affects power transmission and can lead to operational issues.
 
• Regular maintenance and inspection are essential to avoid axle-joint failure and ensure proper vehicle performance.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Bearing Damage:**

 
 
• Bearings support the wheel and axle but are less likely to cause clanking noises.
 
• Damaged bearings usually result in grinding or humming noises.
 
 
 
• **Crack in Axle:**
 
 
• Cracks in the axle can lead to failure but typically do not cause clanking noises during gear engagement.
 
• They may result in vibrations or loss of structural integrity.
 
 
 
• **Bending in Shaft:**
 
 
• Bending can cause misalignment and vibrations but not clanking sounds.
 
• It affects the smooth rotation of the axle.
